items.heading: The Work Is Real
items.text: The work is real and there is a lot of it: thousands of protected sites, many digs to document, many objects to conserve. The weak point is money and paid seats. The people who can pay you are few, and most of them are public bodies.

items.heading: These Figures Come From Official
items.text: These figures come from official documents or from news reports of parliamentary replies. They are the best public picture we could find. Each row says where it comes from.

items.heading: We Lead with the Routes
items.text: We lead with the routes where one skill can grow into work that does not depend on one employer's budget. The crowded and government-only routes stay on the list, marked with their risk. Each row has one of our three ratings.

rows: Entry post at ASI: Assistant Archaeologist
150 posts for 2026, subject to change with workload. Pay Level 6.
ASI draft recruitment rules sent for comments, dated 20 April 2026.
The main central entry door is a few hundred posts at most in any cycle. This is a draft, so read the final rules.
ASI archaeology cadre, filled versus empty
191 vacant out of 420 sanctioned. Conservation cadre: 447 vacant out of 831.
Lok Sabha written reply, reported by ThePrint on 4 August 2026.
Posts exist and are empty. An empty post is not the same as a hiring drive, because rules, court cases and budgets decide when it is filled.
67 posts advertised in 2024. 1,407 applied, 293 shortlisted. About 75 of 120 sanctioned posts unfilled.
ThePrint, 14 July 2026. The advertisement is in court, with serving staff arguing the posts belong to internal promotion.
Getting in is one competition. Moving up is a second, slower queue that is stuck in litigation.
UGC NET June 2026, Archaeology (subject 067), unreserved category
JRF cut-off 212 marks (3 candidates). Assistant Professor cut-off 184 (53). PhD-only cut-off 162 (108).
NTA subject-wise cut-off list, June 2026 session.
The national pool of qualifiers in this subject is tiny, and a funded JRF is rarer still.
